children: Pantheon Macroeconomics has lifted its near-term projections for both growth and inflation after a run of firmer data. The firm still looks for the current burst of momentum to fade in the months ahead.

August’s strong payroll gain is viewed as temporary rather than the start of a lasting hiring acceleration. Unemployment is expected to drift higher as labor-market slack gradually reappears. Upside risks to the outlook have clearly increased, yet Pantheon continues to expect the Federal Reserve to leave policy unchanged while activity and price pressures ease.

A combination of better-than-expected activity readings, the solid August employment report, a renewed jump in energy prices, and a more hawkish tone from the Fed has challenged the consultancy’s earlier dovish stance. The firm added that officials could still deliver one more hike before year-end if a hot inflation print or another robust jobs number unnerves them.

Pantheon’s base case, however, remains that the FOMC stays on hold over the next couple of quarters. That view rests on an anticipated slowdown in consumer spending, the judgment that August’s payroll surge will prove a false dawn, and emerging evidence that the underlying trend in core inflation is becoming more reassuring.

title: Pantheon Macro highlights higher upside risks but still sees the Fed remaining on hold
